extracted.intended_audience: readers of political theory, scholars, and policymakers interested in comparative government and the effects of administrative organisation
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative principles for judging centralisation of government and local (provincial/township) administration, focusing on political effects, advantages, disadvantages, and institutional safeguards in democratic societies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish two kinds of centralisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain interests are common to all parts of a nation (general laws, foreign relations) while others are peculiar to parts of the nation (township business). When power directing general interests is centred, that is central government; when power directing local interests is brought together, that is a central administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify objects within the province of each kind of centralisation to distinguish them; recognise that they may coalesce but are not inseparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid union of central government and centralized administration
rubrics_metrics.description: A central government united to administrative centralisation acquires immense power and accustoms men to set their own will aside, producing habitual submission in every respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The union of these two kinds of centralisation both subdues by force and alters ordinary habits of life; it can submerge individual and collective initiative and is therefore politically dangerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central administration enervates public spirit (long-term harm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Central administration enervates nations by diminishing their public spirit; it may secure transient victories but gradually relaxes the sinews of strength and cannot ensure durable prosperity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh short-term administrative successes against long-term loss of civic energy and renewal of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralisation provides uniformity and prevention but limits action and citizen initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralisation imparts admirable regularity to routine business, represses petty disorder, and excels more in prevention than in action; its force deserts it when society must be disturbed or accelerated and when private cooperation is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider that centralised systems maintain stability and precision but may be impotent when broad citizen cooperation or flexible action is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local administration fosters civic energy and private initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Because administrative authority is within reach of citizens and represents them to some degree, it excites neither jealousy nor hatred and encourages private exertions that, joined to public authorities, often perform what an energetic central administration could not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate systems by how well they encourage citizens to plan, execute, and support public works (schools, worship places, roads) and to feel personal pride in national welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provincial institutions are essential for democratic peoples
rubrics_metrics.description: Provincial (local) institutions are more necessary in proportion as the social condition becomes more democratic; they teach citizens to use freedom in small concerns and provide security against both mob license and absolute power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For democracies, prioritize development and preservation of provincial liberties to train citizens and check concentration of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracies tend to centralise power (creep risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: The constant tendency of democratic nations is to concentrate all the strength of government in the hands of the power which represents the people; once it possesses attributes of government, it tends to penetrate administrative details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be vigilant to avoid the slide from popular representation to administrative domination; historic revolutions can combine impulses to liberty and to despotism.

rubrics_metrics.name: When matters materially affect the state's existence, prefer appointed, removable officers
rubrics_metrics.description: In what materially affects its existence, the government should be served by officers of its own, appointed by itself, removable at pleasure, and accustomed to rapid methods of proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appointed, disciplined administrative agents (rather than only local, elected agents) for urgent or existential state functions to permit swift, coherent action; balance this with local independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of central administrative agents limits issuance of general regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: As the state has no administrative functionaries stationed across its territory, it rarely attempts to issue general police regulations; this lack is severely felt and often observed by Europeans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge trade-offs: decentralisation can impede uniform regulation (e.g., policing, tax collection), producing visible disorder though not necessarily anarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralised enforcement can still be effective via citizen participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Though the United States lacks a state police and has fewer magistrates and prosecutors, crime rarely eludes punishment because everyone feels interested in providing evidence and stopping delinquents; spontaneous committees form to pursue criminals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess law enforcement outcomes not only by institutional centralisation but also by civic willingness to enforce norms and assist prosecutions (e.g., grand juries, local prosecutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralisation may produce social order without happiness or improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: A completely central administration (example: China) can produce peace without happiness, industry without improvement, stability without strength, and public order without public morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating centralised regimes, consider qualitative outcomes (morality, innovation, happiness) as well as order and stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local administrative disorder may coexist with essential guarantees being strong
rubrics_metrics.description: Although lesser details of police and municipal accounts may be neglected in America, the essential guarantees of man in society (fundamental rights) are as strong there as elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate evaluation of minor administrative deficiencies from assessment of fundamental political guarantees; minor neglects do not imply collapse of essential liberties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political advantages of local system outweigh some administrative inefficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Even admitting that remote authority might govern townships more usefully and securely, the political advantages (citizen attachment, pride, active private undertakings) derived from local systems lead to preferring them to remote centralisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh civic and political benefits (engagement, attachment to nation) against gains in efficiency when considering decentralisation vs centralisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central oversight of local administration is desirable without active interference
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority which represents the state ought not to waive the right of inspecting the local administration; an agent to prosecute misdemeanors of township and county officers would produce more uniform order without compromising township independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design oversight mechanisms that promote uniformity and accountability while preserving local autonomy; be mindful of cultural resistance to 'public informers' and provide alternative institutional remedies (e.g., grand juries, local prosecutors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional safeguards (local prosecutors, grand juries) enable accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions exist in states appointing local officers to conduct public prosecutions at state expense and assembling grand juries several times a year, giving aggrieved persons access and ensuring complaints, particularly against public officers, are investigated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement and evaluate institutional mechanisms at the local level to ensure checks on local officials—these can substitute for intrusive central agents while maintaining effectiveness.
